rows.subtype: Wow, ooh and ah in messages [Mismatch]
rows.description: A young adult reads wow in a text as admiration, shock or sarcasm depending on tone and emoji. Without a voice the reader can misjudge, so clear words or a follow-up call keep sarcasm from causing hurt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, surprise, hurt

rows.subtype: Louder, higher voice in excitement or anger [Interpreting]
rows.description: A young adult hears friends speak louder and higher when excited and sometimes the same when angry. Words, face and context decide; the wise response to a raised angry voice is to stay calm and step back if unsafe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger, excitement, calm, trust

rows.subtype: Varying pitch for persuasion and presentation [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult varies pitch and pace to keep listeners engaged in a debate or interview, and avoids sounding flat. Natural variety builds trust, while artificial theatrics can seem insincere.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: interest, resentment, trust

rows.description: A young adult in a presentation or interview who speaks with a resonant, steady voice usually signals composure, though nervous people can also sound steady. Breath and posture help build the effect honestly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, resentment, relief from stress

rows.description: A listener hearing a trembling voice from a colleague or student may assume fear, grief, anger or excitement. The wise reading is to wait, stay warm and ask, rather than assume weakness or deception.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: grief, anger, fear, excitement

rows.subtype: Measured pace in interviews and presentations [Regulating]
rows.description: A young adult in an interview or seminar who keeps a measured pace with deliberate pauses appears organized. Slowing too much may read as disinterest, so pace should fit the room and topic.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: Speech rhythm differs across Indian languages, accents and English varieties, so a fast or sing-song rhythm may be normal for the speaker. Judging intelligence or attitude from rhythm alone is a common and unfair pitfall.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult in negotiation or interview may use a brief pause to think or let a point land. A long silence can feel like pressure in some cultures and respect in others, so the setting guides use.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Chanting, devotional singing and protest songs [Mismatch]
rows.description: A young adult may chant or sing in devotion, a stadium or a protest for solidarity, faith or grief. The same rhythm can signal joy or anger, so context and respect for the group matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: joy, admiration, grief, anger

rows.description: A young adult in an interview or new college introduces self with name, role and a short line about interests. Confident, clear greetings build trust, and norms differ across cultures for title use and eye contact.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
